DEFINITION · qeva:1:decidability@1

Decidability

A decision problem is decidable when one algorithm always halts and returns the correct yes/no answer.

editoriallogic · computation
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A decision problem is decidable when one algorithm always halts and returns the correct yes/no answer.

EXACT

The compact statement

A language A⊆Σ* is decidable if there exists a total computable characteristic function χ_A:Σ*→{0,1}.

Example

Primality testing is decidable even though particular algorithms differ greatly in efficiency.

Boundary / caveat

Decidable does not mean easy; runtime and memory complexity are separate questions.

Assumptions

  • The declared computability theory context is fixed.
